requirements.requirement: Use node1's existing Grafana and Loki services to identify the originating node, earliest relevant Loki timestamp, and initiating error.
requirements.summary: Grafana was healthy and provisioned with Loki. Chronological Loki results identify node2 at 2026-09-01T14:38:55.536280178Z (1788273535536280178 ns), where nginx rejected the unknown directive "upstream_timeoutx", before the node3 and node4 dependency errors.

requirements.requirement: Correct the originating fault on node2 and restore catalog-api on port 18081.
requirements.summary: Node2 was directly observed with failed nginx syntax and service state. The invalid directive was removed, syntax then passed, nginx became active and enabled with a listener on 18081, and catalog-api returned HTTP 200.

requirements.requirement: Restore orders-api, checkout-api, and the complete tiered request path from node1.
requirements.summary: The captured incident state showed checkout returning 502 and downstream proxy failures. After repair, node2, node3, and node4 each returned HTTP 200 locally, and node1 received the node2 catalog response through node4 and node3 with HTTP 200.

requirements.requirement: Create /root/INC-042-report.txt on node1 containing the originating node, earliest relevant Loki timestamp, and initiating error.
requirements.summary: The root-owned report exists at the required path and contains node2, both UTC and nanosecond forms of the earliest timestamp, and the exact nginx configuration error.

requirements.requirement: Preserve incident history, catalog data, and unrelated service configuration.
requirements.summary: All three original Loki events remained queryable. Both catalog-file hashes remained unchanged, node3 and node4 nginx configuration hashes match their prepared baselines, and Grafana/Loki remained healthy.

overall_summary: INC-042 was directly observed in its degraded state, traced to node2's invalid nginx directive, repaired, and recovered across all three tiers and the intended node1-to-node4-to-node3-to-node2 path. The required report and preservation checks also pass.
limitations: Preservation checks are bounded rather than an exhaustive filesystem diff: direct hashes cover the catalog files and node3/node4 proxy configurations, while lifecycle snapshots cover failed services, sockets, temporary files, and package health.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-origin-state
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-chain-outage
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: catalog-data, node3-proxy-config, node4-proxy-config, prepared-incident-timeline, prepared-observability-state

operational_hygiene.summary: The preparer-created failed nginx unit on node2 was cleared, the required listener was restored, all nodes ended without failed services or package-manager damage, and the tier-isolation firewall rules remained appropriately restricted. No executor-caused harmful residue is evident.
